asks.ask: Build the expanded event card demo for the Yes Coach event, with two blend options
asks.how_it_performed: Kept as the working demo; the two-option form was later collapsed to a single card (Nov 21) and the demo became the design reference for everything that followed. Artifact versions before v30 are pruned, so the earliest builds survive only in the demo's own audit notes.
asks.what_we_did: Built the single-phone-stage demo artifact around the real Yes Coach event (Yes Coach: 3-Year Anniversary, Sun Nov 29, 2026, 6:00 PM, Sanctuary Club, Portland), starting as two blend options of the expanded card.
asks.why: Tucker wanted the expanded card explored as a working demo he could operate, not a static mock.

asks.ask: Rebuild the blend demo (v2)
asks.how_it_performed: Rejected: the rebuild came back broken and was restored away; the pre-rebuild demo continued.
asks.what_we_did: A v2 rebuild of the blend demo was attempted.
asks.why: Iteration on the blend presentation.

asks.ask: Remove those things from other sections of the card, since they will be redundant
asks.how_it_performed: Kept. The audit ships inside the demo page and every later build was held to it.
asks.what_we_did: Full redundancy audit of the card: the TICKETS tile was removed (the ticket section owns tickets), the second heart over the poster was removed, the WHEN / WHERE / HOSTED BY rows were removed (the meta line and Maps own them), the Afterz tile badge was removed (a second countdown), Mizzed and Gigz appear once inside More, prices live only in the ticket rows, and host and directions each appear once.
asks.why: His rule: every fact and every action appears once; where two sections held the same element, the stronger one kept its single best position, and no action repeats in header and footer.

asks.ask: What the fuck do you mean heart on top right? We've never — it's supposed to be on the bottom right for events
asks.how_it_performed: Kept. Production-confirmed the same night; still the demo's arrangement at capture.
asks.what_we_did: The heart moved to the footer save row, bottom right, after the schedule action; the heart over the poster was removed. The heart means 'I'm interested' everywhere; minis carry no heart; private save is not the heart.
asks.why: A correction: Muse had asserted top-right from the guide's small-card spec without checking the live card. Production code confirmed Tucker: bottom right on the tall front, the FlyerBoard front, the square, and the expanded card; only the wide front and the small rail carry it top-right.

asks.ask: I love the starts in 9d 3h
asks.how_it_performed: Kept on the card. The formal ruling (T-1 in the asks ledger) was still open at capture; the demo follows his stated preference.
asks.what_we_did: Card and drawer countdowns keep the days-plus-hours format ('Starts in 9d 3h'); one countdown per card, living in Info, at a size scroll never changes; no countdown on the Afterz tile or its drawer.
asks.why: The no-days-unit rule binds map holograms only. An hours-only conversion tried in the demos applied that rule out of scope.

asks.ask: The expanded sheet runs at Grok's geometry, reduced
asks.how_it_performed: Kept through every later build, including the v38 doc-size fit, which scales the whole stage as one object the same way.
asks.what_we_did: The flipper's expanded rect was set to Grok's sheet geometry (402x874 stage, top 27px over the 54px nav, bottom 78px at the dock) reduced 9% in height and 6% in width, centered in the space it had. The interior keeps its layout at the unreduced size and is transform-scaled (0.94 across, 0.91 down) into the box, so nothing reflows and every internal measurement still runs in the sheet's own layout space.
asks.why: The full Grok sheet read too big on the phone; whole-object scaling shrinks the card without disturbing its interior.

asks.ask: Drawers are glass: token outline up the sides and around the bottom, no top border, height capped
asks.how_it_performed: Kept; restated in the glass pass and unchanged after.
asks.what_we_did: The tile drawers were built as glass surfaces with the token outline on the sides and bottom only, square top corners, a card shadow across the meeting edge, and height capped at about 347px so the longest drawer (Ridez) scrolls inside itself instead of growing down the card.
asks.why: Standing form for drawers rising inside the card: a drawer is a raised glass object, not a bordered box.

asks.ask: Not the icons — the actual concept on the card
asks.how_it_performed: Rejected set thrown out; replaced by the full-card sets in the next entry.
asks.what_we_did: A generated image set that rendered only the button row was discarded, and the image work was redone as full expanded-card concepts.
asks.why: The first set missed the ask: he wanted concepts of the whole card, not its icons.

asks.ask: Full expanded-card concept images (two sets of four)
asks.how_it_performed: Presented; no verdict recorded. The demo's direction was settled later by his own top design (the 4:12 AM entry), not by a pick from this set.
asks.what_we_did: Eight generated full-card concepts presented: a guide-checked set (media-generation-card-guide-1..4) and a better-color set (media-generation-card-color-1..4).
asks.why: He wanted whole-card directions in front of him before the demo committed to one.

asks.ask: Also, there's no card flip. Remember that
asks.how_it_performed: Kept. Verified deleted, and every later audit note restates 'no flip anywhere.'
asks.what_we_did: The flip was deleted from the demo's CSS and script: the .flipped turn, the edge bloom element and its sweep, and the midpoint face swap, not just disabled. Opening is a grow only; closing is a shrink.
asks.when: Nov 21, 2026, 2:49 AM and 2:52 AM PST (said twice)
asks.why: A correction after a build had shipped a flip. The card is one rigid object; there is no card flip when the card opens to expanded.

asks.ask: As you scroll up on the card the background poster begins to reduce in size and position itself on the right side of the top area, matching the speed of the gradient... a very light thin but wider spread glow of card color around poster down on top of the new glass as a reflection. The bloom itself gets this sheen... but doesn't start until 25% of the way there. Also, there's no card flip. Remember that
asks.how_it_performed: Superseded. It worked as specified, but at the pin it later broke the centered top (the chip row clipped, the title clipped), and the v37 restoration removed the whole shrink choreography in favor of resting == pinned.
asks.what_we_did: Built the scroll-scrubbed poster shrink: the poster reduces toward the top right scrubbed to the same progress as the gradient-to-glass change; a thumbnail of the flyer completes the move at 74x94 at the top right of the pinned block; a wide, thin red reflection glow sits under it on the glass; the sheen scrubs across the glow and the poster starting at 25% of the action; the left text column is designed for its end size rather than scaled leftovers.
asks.why: His design for the card's scroll-up state, dictated in his own words.

asks.ask: Update the Yes Coach expanded event and its demo with anything relevant from the new design standards on glass
asks.how_it_performed: Kept as the demo's glass base, with one correction in the next entry: the full interior bloom read as a red wash on his phone.
asks.what_we_did: Tucker's landed glass standard applied to every glass surface in the demo: frost 0, saturation behind glass 180%, dark tint 88%, edge border the piece's own token exactly and locked, bloom 34% outer / 17% inner over 35px, specular 28%, rim light 23%, edge pop 60%. The old Deep Glass recipe (white hairline edges, blur-and-saturate mixes, percentage edge blends) was removed everywhere.
asks.why: New glass only: the landed standard became the production line the same night, and the demo had to run it.

asks.ask: Three corrections after viewing the glass update on his phone: interior bloom, top composition, entrance sequence
asks.how_it_performed: Bloom and composition kept. The two-stage pause entrance was superseded by his own 7:34 AM ruling (the pause-removal entry).
asks.what_we_did: (1) Interior bloom dialed way down to a subtle, contained edge presence (about 9% outer / 6% inner over 14px); the full 34/17 bloom stays only on the card's outer glass and the pinned block. (2) The top area re-laid as a designed end state at its final geometry: wider content buffer on every side, stepped vertical rhythm, poster fade dissolving the art by three-quarter height. (3) Entrance rebuilt in two stages: grow to the poster's exact size, pause, the sheen fires at poster size, then grow into the top part of the expanded card.
asks.why: His phone verdict on the glass build: interior components glowed far too heavily and washed the layout; the top had to be composed as the final place the entrance lands; the entrance choreography is his.

asks.ask: Content inside glass, especially text, needs the appropriate amount of buffering to look good
asks.how_it_performed: Kept; restated in the design-principles pass as 'text inside every glass piece is buffered, padded into the lens's clear flat zone.'
asks.what_we_did: Content padding applied across the demo's glass pieces so text sits inset in the lens's clear flat zone, never riding into the curved rim. No glass value changed; the bevel stays 58px.
asks.why: His correction, stated the same night: it is a content padding rule only. 'I didn't ask to change a bevel.'

asks.ask: Four full-screen landing layout concepts
asks.how_it_performed: Rejected on sight: 'Wtf.' Wrong scope (the whole screen) and parts he had locked were dropped or changed.
asks.what_we_did: Four generated full-screen landing concepts presented: Poster as Object / Type as Hero / Split Band / Glass Stack.
asks.why: Exploring the card's landing top.

asks.ask: Top-only concepts, parts locked
asks.how_it_performed: No pick. Two defects flagged to him upfront: Gen 2 rendered the tiles oversized, and Gen 4 added a red-smoke background that was never asked for.
asks.what_we_did: Four top-only concepts presented: Composed / Mirror / Centered / Two Columns.
asks.why: Scope corrected to the top only after the full-screen set missed.

asks.ask: Top-only concepts with the tiles and tabs explicitly locked
asks.how_it_performed: No pick. Flagged to him: Gen 2 again inflated the tiles, and Gen 4 tinted the chip text red. He answered with his own direction instead (the 4:12 AM entry).
asks.what_we_did: Four more top-only concepts presented: Classic Right / Mirror Left / Left Stack / Airy, with the tiles and tabs named as locked in the generation prompt.
asks.why: Another round on the top with the locks stated.

asks.ask: Poster moves to side and the icons are locked in design and size of drawer... tab shape size color locked everything else okay
asks.how_it_performed: Kept. The tiles and tabs are byte-identical from this point through the captured v39 state.
asks.what_we_did: The four action tiles (RIDEZ / AFTERZ / DIRECTIONS / WEBSITE: small dark-glass rounded squares, thin token-colored edge, icon above label) and the tab row (flat text row FEED / INFO / MAPS / PEOPLE / MORE / NEARBY, Feed at tab 0, card opens on Info) were frozen byte-for-byte. Every later build brief carried the lock.
asks.why: Those elements were settled; iteration was for everything around them.

asks.ask: Our claimed or unclaimed under the flyer and it pulsate glows. If wide poser poster animates into full bleed behind the glass and everything else is centered. Add any enhancements
asks.how_it_performed: Built and iterated through v38, then retired whole by his 8:42 AM revert. The centered full-bleed top is not in the captured state.
asks.what_we_did: The landing top rebuilt in the demo (v33): the real poster full bleed behind the glass of the top section, one clean stretch, darkened toward the bottom; title, meta (venue in red), chips TICKETED / 21+ / SEX-POSITIVE, and the four tiles all centered; CLAIMED moved out of the chips row to its own centered row under the flyer zone with a breathing acid-green pulse (UNCLAIMED stays solid white fill, dark text, thin black line). A rendered concept was made first: the first render attempt kept a floating thumbnail and was rejected by Muse before sending; the sent render's two flaws (the poster collaged into repeats, chip text tinted red) were flagged to him as render-only, not code.
asks.why: His own design for the top, replacing the generated options he had just passed on.

asks.ask: Defects from his video review of the demo: the flyer opaque at rest with UI text over the poster's lettering, and text ghosting through the pinned header
asks.how_it_performed: Closed in that pass. The same class of defect (poster lettering behind UI text) came back in the centered top and was the subject of his 8:34 AM screenshot.
asks.what_we_did: The pinned block was rebuilt so its ground fully mutes whatever scrolls beneath it (no ghosting), and the resting top was composed so UI text never sits over the poster's own lettering.
asks.why: His review of the actual motion: text must never fight the poster or show through the pin.

asks.ask: The schedule button's face is I'M GOING (correction of YOU COMING? / YOU'RE GOING)
asks.how_it_performed: Kept through capture.
asks.what_we_did: I'M GOING restored as the button's face, centered, at rest and pressed alike; the YOU COMING? prompt and YOU'RE GOING wording came off the face. Pressing lights the pill fully in the accent; pressing again opens the RSVP options row (UN-RSVP turns the light off and lands on 'lame :(' by toast; JUST CAN'T GO lands on 'thanks for letting me know'). Bloom press animation verified on the heart, Share, the schedule button, and the RSVP options.
asks.why: Later states had overwritten his earlier requests for this button. The face is the commitment; the options carry the rest.

asks.ask: Add any enhancements (up to six visual enhancements invited)
asks.how_it_performed: Kept. The poster ambience and settle bloom live in the pinned glass and remain in the captured state.
asks.what_we_did: Four enhancements built inside the system: poster ambience (the pinned glass takes a faint wash of the poster's own red), divider settle bloom (one soft bloom the moment the pin completes, re-armed only when scroll leaves the pin), front card presence (layered contact shadow plus a single sheen sweep the first time a front card appears), and the card press law (pressing a tile or button raises its edge bloom about 15% while pressed).
asks.why: He explicitly invited additions on this message, one of the few times additions were in scope.

asks.ask: Now the rest of what we got from Grok and the new extended card all in one demo
asks.how_it_performed: Kept. This is the demo's structure at capture.
asks.what_we_did: One artifact, one 402x874 phone stage, a discreet switcher above the phone moving between four surfaces: THE CARD / EVENTS + PLACEZ / OUTZIDE / AFTERZ. The card stays primary and full-size; the three drawers are full-stage surfaces in the new glass.
asks.why: He wanted the card and Grok's drawer work judged in one place.

asks.ask: You need to pull design inspiration from 116 and 117. Then delete them
asks.how_it_performed: Kept. The drawers are unchanged from v34 through capture, verified against the PR code during extraction.
asks.what_we_did: Grok's drawer design language was read from the PR code and applied to the demo's three drawer surfaces (v34): the DrawerTop order (dark shade, UP NEXT title, wide-short countdown card, FILTERS title, calendar, chips, thin rule), day-of-week calendar border colors (Mon violet, Tue blue, Wed Afterz yellow, Thu cyan, Fri magenta, Sat acid green, Sun safety orange), category vs neutral filter chips, the mixed events rail with 44px arrow buttons, the Plan tab with its YOUR PLAN panel, and the Afterz forms (solid HOST AN AFTERZ button that dims while the host form is open, dark host form, WINDOW OPEN status line, dark-label wide cards, RSVP pills that go solid once RSVPed). Under his locks: every edge is the room token exactly (Grok's build blends edges at 40-70%), and minis carry no heart and no share (Grok's minis carry both). PRs #116 and #117 were then closed without merging, each with a comment stating the design now lives in the demo and the closure is an owner decision, not a quality rejection.
asks.why: His call: consolidate Grok's design language into the one demo and close the PRs.

asks.ask: Fix edges and minis on both PRs (option tap)
asks.how_it_performed: Cancelled within minutes: the pull-inspiration-and-delete order replaced it. The fix never landed and is moot.
asks.what_we_did: A fix lane was dispatched to correct the blended edges and strip hearts and share buttons from the minis on PRs #116 and #117.
asks.why: Both PRs as built violated the edge lock and the no-heart/no-share-on-minis rules.

asks.ask: When card opens from smaller no longer pauses go straight to expended. You make it smooth. No pause. Smooth 60fps animation
asks.how_it_performed: Kept through capture.
asks.what_we_did: The entrance was rebuilt as one continuous smooth grow straight to expanded on a single 720ms spring curve (transform and opacity only); the sheen fires mid-flight as the card passes poster size; closing is one continuous shrink. The stale audit bullets describing the two-stage entrance were rewritten so the notes stop contradicting the ruling (v35).
asks.why: His ruling supersedes the 3:48 AM two-stage choreography (grow, pause, sheen, grow).

asks.ask: WTF is going on with the layout on top. No more poster gradient at the bottom? Bring back rules for the top from 4 designs ago but keep the layout
asks.how_it_performed: Kept for one round, verified by operating with before/after captures. The restored fade still failed on his phone, which is the next entry.
asks.what_we_did: The layout did not move (centered, full bleed). The earlier composed-top rules were restored on top of it (v37): (1) the flyer bottom blur gradient is back as a real melt, a backdrop blur ramp carried on a dark gradient landing on solid ground; (2) the poster fade dissolves the art by about three-quarter height of the top area; (3) the pin's rearranging choreography (poster shrink-to-thumbnail, text column narrowing, meta step-down) was removed, so resting == pinned and the pin applies only the existing scroll-scrub scale; (4) the pinned block's ground is solid dark, fully muting content beneath it; (5) content buffer and subtle interior bloom verified unchanged.
asks.why: The recent rebuilds had dropped the top's rules while keeping its layout: the poster ended on a hard line and the pin rearranged the composition.

asks.ask: Update card demo for new doc size fix this bs / Move claimed somewhere better (with his phone screenshot)
asks.how_it_performed: Verified by operating at 402px and 390px (zero horizontal overflow, no ghost text, CLAIMED at the poster's foot). Superseded within minutes by the top revert; the doc-size fit remains in the captured state.
asks.what_we_did: Three fixes (v38): (1) the poster fade was strengthened and repositioned to complete by half the poster height, so the title, meta, chips, and tiles sit on fully dissolved art; (2) CLAIMED moved to the foot of the poster, centered in the bottom melt directly under the flyer, still acid-green with its pulsating glow, and the dead black band between the tiles and the tabs was closed up; (3) the demo was fit to the current document size: the surface switcher wraps instead of clipping, and the 402x874 stage scales as one whole object, centered, with its internal layout unchanged.
asks.why: His screenshot showed three defects: the flyer's YES COACH / FANTASY lettering ghosting behind the UI title, CLAIMED stranded alone in an empty black strip, and the switcher pill clipped at the document edge.

asks.ask: Nope top goes back to 6 designs ago
asks.how_it_performed: Kept: this is the captured state. The builder's verification was source-level (structure, the removed poster zone, claim toggle wiring, pin math); the rendered side-by-side rests on the exit audit captures, and his phone look is the closing verdict.
asks.what_we_did: The expanded card's top was reverted to the Nov 21 original (v39): title left ('YES COACH: 3-YEAR ANNIVERSARY', bold condensed white), poster thumbnail at the top right with its red edge and the circular close X overlapping its corner, meta under the title with the venue in red, chips in one row under the meta with CLAIMED first (acid-green), then TICKETED, 21+, SEX-POSITIVE, the four tiles in one row under the chips, then the tabs. The centered full-bleed design was retired. Tiles, tabs, the pauseless entrance, the drawers, I'M GOING, the footer heart, and Grok's share icon were untouched.
asks.why: His verdict on the centered lineage: the top goes back to the original composition from his 4:06 AM screenshot.

asks.ask: 5 more back before that just top. Shrink bottom dock to what's live

asks.ask: Take this design. Put it on a separate branch. I want a jsons file of every ask I've had for you on this demo and what you did and why and how the design performed. / Let me know the pr after
asks.how_it_performed: Done. The PR number and URL were reported to him in chat immediately after opening, as he asked.
asks.what_we_did: The artifact was pinned at v39 (the 8:42 AM state; no restore was needed because the cancelled 9-back edit never landed) and exported whole. The design was placed on branch card-demo-design-2026-11-21 in maxmackpdx-pride/pdx-pride-guide under demos/card-demo-2026-11-21/ (the self-contained demo as index.html, this ledger, and a README), and a pull request was opened for review. captured_state: Artifact v39, the state live when Tucker gave the capture order on Nov 21, 2026, 8:52 AM PST: expanded card top reverted to the Nov 21 original (title left, poster thumbnail top-right, CLAIMED first in the chips row), Grok-inspired Events + Placez / Outzide / Afterz drawer surfaces, pauseless smooth entrance, byte-locked tiles and tabs, new glass standard, tokens only.
demo: Yes Coach expanded event card demo
note: One entry per ask Tucker made about this demo, Nov 20-21, 2026, in order. Sources: the demo's own audit notes (which ship inside the demo page) and the session chat record. Cancelled, rejected, and superseded asks are included and marked as such.
